why: In A there are three shapes: square, circle inside it, and an arrow. In B the middle shape (the square) is removed from around the circle and becomes a small shape at the tail of the arrow, and the arrow becomes straight and points the opposite way. In C the circle is the middle shape, so it goes to the tail of a straight arrow inside the square, and the arrow now points left. Option 4 shows exactly this. Option 1 is tempting but it keeps the circle and puts the square on the tail, which is the wrong way round.
trick: List the shapes in A and B, see which one moved where, then move the same-position shape in C.
note: Curved arrows in A and C are blurry in the scan; drawn simplified (bent tail, curved shaft, head up-left in A and up-right in C).
